sub.en: Look at each pair. What happens to the object of the active sentence?

items.q: Cans ___ in 1810.
items.why: The passive is be + the past participle. The object of the active sentence becomes the subject, and the doer disappears — or comes back after by.

items.q: The bread ___ in a wood oven.
One third of the world’s food ___ away.
Cans were invented ___ a French chef.
items.why: by tells you WHO did it: invented by a chef.

items.q: Paper is made ___ wood.
items.why: made FROM = the material has changed completely (paper from wood). made OF = you can still see it (a bottle made of glass).

items.q: Water ___ in coconut shells.
These spring rolls ___ at room temperature.
It’s worth ___ the label before you throw it away.
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 28: after “it’s worth”, the -ing form.

items.from: A French chef invented cans in 1810.
items.cue: Make it passive — the chef doesn’t matter

items.a: The bread is baked here every morning

They were invented by a French chef

tts: Millions of years ago, people hunted for food and ate it immediately. But they soon realized they could keep their food for longer if they protected it.
So the world’s first food containers were made from animal skins and large leaves. Water was kept in coconut shells and dried vegetable skins.
Metal containers — or cans — were invented in 1810 by a French chef called Monsieur Appert. The Emperor Napoleon offered a prize to anybody who could find a way of keeping food fresh for his army.

items.q: What did people do at first?
The first containers were made from
Water was kept in
Cans were invented in
They were invented by
Why did Napoleon offer a prize?
o: to keep food fresh for his army

tts: A recent report has found that one third of the world’s food ends up in the rubbish bin. Here in the UK, half of the food which is thrown away comes from our homes.
Much of the waste happens because people buy too much food, which they don’t have time to cook. The food is just left at the back of the fridge or the cupboard and then it’s forgotten.
Another reason is that people don’t understand the labels. “Best before” is about quality; “use by” is about safety. A lot of good food is thrown away on the wrong day.

items.s: One third of the world’s food ends up in the bin.
In the UK, half of the wasted food comes from homes.
People waste food because they buy too little.

acts.title: From the field to the shelf
text: A tin of tomatoes costs about the same as three fresh ones and lasts two years. This is how that happens.

The tomatoes are grown in southern Italy and picked in August, almost all of it by machine. They are washed, and the skins are removed with steam rather than by hand. Then they are packed into tins that were made in a different factory, sealed, and heated to about 120 degrees for a few minutes. That last step is the whole invention: the heat kills everything, and because the tin is already closed, nothing can get back in.
The method was invented in 1810 by a French chef, and it was not improved in any important way for a hundred and fifty years.
The tin is then labelled, boxed and transported, and transportation is where most of the cost is. The tomatoes themselves are the cheapest part of the tin you are holding.

items.s: The tomatoes are grown in southern Italy.
They are picked mostly by hand.
The skins are removed with steam.
The tins are made in the same factory.
The heating happens after the tin is closed.
Transportation is where most of the cost is.

write.q: Describe how something is made or done — a dish, a product, or a process at your work: 6 sentences. Use the passive at least four times, one “made from”, and one past passive with a date.
write.model: Beshbarmak is made from meat, flour, water and onions, and almost nothing else. The meat is boiled slowly for two or three hours and the water is kept, because the broth is served with it. While that happens, the dough is rolled out very thin and cut into wide flat squares. The squares are boiled in the same broth. Everything is put on one large plate and it is eaten with the hands, which is where the name comes from. The dish was described by travellers in the nineteenth century in almost exactly the same way.

speak.q: Explain out loud how a dish from your country is made, in five steps. Use the passive at least three times, and finish with one fact using “was invented” or “was made”.
speak.model: The meat is boiled for two hours. The broth is kept. The dough is rolled very thin and cut into squares. The squares are boiled in the broth. Everything is served on one plate. The dish was described by travellers two hundred years ago in the same way.
